channel.title: New research | AI & Attention Observatory
channel.description: New studies and ideas about AI, cognition, and attention. Research notes link to the original evidence.

item.title: Shutting down AI with a single switch may be less realistic than designing systems that remain governable.
item.description: Perspective: Shutting down AI with a single switch may be less realistic than designing systems that remain governable. A kill switch to shut down dangerous AI systems is a seductive concept, but the metaphor hides how the models work – and how they get out of control in the first place.

item.title: Both SRLbot and Emotional SRLbot were associated with higher self‐reported enjoyment and lower boredom than ChatGPT and elicited trace‐based SRL behaviours.
item.description: Research finding: Both SRLbot and Emotional SRLbot were associated with higher self‐reported enjoyment and lower boredom than ChatGPT and elicited trace‐based SRL behaviours.

item.title: AI assistance may gradually shift from supporting thinking to replacing it.
item.description: Research question: AI assistance may gradually shift from supporting thinking to replacing it. An argument about cognitive deskilling distinguishes complementary help from taking over essential reasoning.

item.title: Stress and social-media time stood out as signals of academic difficulty.
item.description: Research finding: Stress and social-media time stood out as signals of academic difficulty. Digital interruptions may matter for attention, but this study did not examine generative AI.

item.title: What makes sustained attention easier or harder?
item.description: Research question: What makes sustained attention easier or harder? This study aimed to investigate the relationship between response time variability and levels of ADHD symptoms both in this new, low-arousal sustained attention task and in the Sustained Attention to Response Task (SART).

item.title: When does AI assistance become cognitive dependence?
item.description: Research question: When does AI assistance become cognitive dependence? Materials comprised interviews with 22 teachers, three documentary cases, self-narratives and reflective essays.

item.title: How do people monitor and regulate their thinking with technology?
item.description: Research question: How do people monitor and regulate their thinking with technology? This theory-building systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on metacognition, trust, and human–AI co-regulation in GenAI-supported foreign language learning.

item.title: Communication depends on listeners as well as speakers; conversational AI changes both sides of that exchange.
item.description: Perspective: Communication depends on listeners as well as speakers; conversational AI changes both sides of that exchange. AI systems tend to focus on the person speaking – but the listener plays just as big a part in communication.

item.title: Fast-moving children’s media can hold the gaze while leaving too little room to think through what is happening.
item.description: Perspective: Fast-moving children’s media can hold the gaze while leaving too little room to think through what is happening. Media quality cannot be reduced to screen-time totals or educational subject matter. Kucirkova argues that the rhythm of children's media shapes opportunities to reflect, understand a story and connect emotionally: constantly shifting cues may capture attention while leaving too little space to process.

item.title: AI support should follow demonstrated learning readiness, rather than replace foundational thinking from the outset.
item.description: Conceptual framework: AI support should follow demonstrated learning readiness, rather than replace foundational thinking from the outset. A proposed staged approach to AI use in formal learning; distinguish foundational independent work from guided and selective offloading.
